hook_text: Long ago, if you wanted to know how important someone was, you looked at their cattle.
clip_script: Ulundi, KwaZulu-Natal. A herd of Nguni cattle: white, red, speckled, grey. In early farming societies, cattle were wealth. They joined families through lobola, and they honoured the ancestors in the kraal. The chief was leader, judge and guardian of the land, and led the first fruits ceremony. He had the biggest herds, and he loaned cattle to poorer families, who became loyal to him. Cattle and power went together.
visual_style: Whiteboard herd of patterned cattle, then two families joined by a line of cattle, then a chief lending cows to homesteads across the hills.
mood: Proud and warm, like a celebration.
pacing: Builds from one herd to a whole chiefdom linked by cattle.
